title: Aggrega Workspace Config
description: Per-workspace configuration file consumed by the aggrega CLI. Lives at `.aggrega-config.yaml` in the workspace root and carries four top-level blocks: workspace (registry/cache/offline settings + CUE-module registry routing), build (authoring-release hint + deprecation strictness dials), plugins (workspace-level Wasm plugin attachments: mutator, policy, linter, importer), and lint (per-rule strictness dials, currently a single `publishing_discipline` block). Workspace-config file (flat top-level shape, no apiVersion/kind envelope) distinct from catalog content. Schema evolution discipline: adding a new top-level block alongside `workspace`/`build`/`plugins`/`lint` is a SemVer-MINOR bump (additive); adding a new flag inside an existing block is likewise a SemVer-MINOR bump; removing a key or tightening a constraint is a SemVer-MAJOR break.

workspace.description: Workspace-level orientation: which registry the build pushes to and pulls from, where the local artifact cache lives, whether the build operates offline, and how CUE-module imports resolve to registries.

default_registry.description: Default OCI registry host the build pushes published artifacts to and pulls dependencies from when an entity does not name a registry explicitly. Defaults to `hub.aggrega.ai`.

catalog_dirs.description: Optional vendored catalog directories the resolver consults before falling back to the registry. Each entry is a filesystem path relative to the workspace root.

cache_dir.description: Local artifact cache directory (registry pulls, OCI manifests, compiled fixtures). Defaults to `.aggrega/cache`. Should be gitignored by convention.

offline.description: When true, the build does not contact any registry; only cached artifacts and vendored catalog content are consulted. Defaults to false.

auto_pull.description: When true (default), `aggrega build` invokes `aggrega pull` in-process whenever the per-release lockfile is missing, so a first-time build against a Release does not require an explicit pull step. When false, missing lockfile halts the build with a diagnostic asking the operator to run pull explicitly. Independent of `offline`: `offline: true` ignores `auto_pull` and always halts on missing lockfile.

cue_registry.description: CUE-module registry routing. `default` is the registry host CUE-module imports resolve through; `overrides` maps prefixes (e.g. `acme.com`) to alternative registry hosts.

default.description: Default registry host for CUE-module imports.

overrides.description: Prefix-based routing overrides. Each entry routes module imports under the named prefix to the named registry.

prefix.description: Module-path prefix this override applies to (e.g. `acme.com`).

registry.description: Registry host imports matching the prefix resolve through.

build.description: Build-time strictness dials and authoring hints. `authoring_release` provides the LSP a `current Release` hint for inline diagnostics; `halt_on_deprecated` and `halt_on_deprecated_severity` (reserved for the deprecation-policy rule) control how the build reacts to deprecated-entity consumption.

authoring_release.description: Path to a Release YAML file the LSP treats as the `current Release` context for inline diagnostics. Optional.

halt_on_deprecated.description: When true, consuming a deprecated entity halts the build (instead of emitting a warning). Reserved for the upcoming deprecation-policy rule; today the loader accepts the key but no rule consumes it yet.

halt_on_deprecated_severity.description: Severity level the deprecation-policy rule emits when `halt_on_deprecated` is true: `error` halts the build, `warning` emits a diagnostic but lets the build proceed. Reserved for the upcoming deprecation-policy rule.

plugins.description: Workspace-level Wasm plugin attachments. Each socket (mutator, policy, linter, importer) takes an array of plugin references; the build invokes each plugin's documented entry function per its socket contract.

lint.description: Per-rule strictness dials. Future lint sub-categories (build-time discouragement, FinOps lint, etc.) land as peer sub-blocks of `publishing_discipline`.

publishing_discipline.description: Workspace-wide gates for the publishing-linter's rule set. `enforce_monotonic_narrowing` and `enforce_immutability` are workspace-wide rule gates (default true each); `narrowing_exemptions` carries per-entity escape hatches for legitimate narrowing cases. The remaining `allow_*` flags relax individual discouragement checks.

enforce_monotonic_narrowing.description: When true (default), the publishing-linter and discouragement walker enforce the monotonic-narrowing rule: a child schema's constraint must narrow (not widen) vs the parent's. Set to false for the rare workspace-wide opt-out; per-entity exemptions are the recommended pattern for legitimate cases.

enforce_immutability.description: When true (default), the publishing-linter enforces the artifact-immutability rule: a published `name:version` plus content digest is treated as final; `aggrega push` rejects overwrites. Set to false only for forensic reproduction of historical builds where overwrites occurred prior to the rule's introduction; routine use is discouraged. Required for production catalogs.

narrowing_exemptions.description: Per-entity exemptions from the narrowing-violation rule. Used when `enforce_monotonic_narrowing` stays true (the default) but specific entity/path pairs need exemption with a documented reason. Each entry names the catalog entity, the specific schema paths exempted, and the human-readable justification.

entity.description: Catalog entity identifier the exemption applies to (e.g. `my-team/datastore/mariadb-eu`).

paths.description: JSON-Pointer-style schema paths the exemption covers (e.g. `spec.schema.values.primary.replicaCount`). Each path is a fully-qualified path into the entity's schema content.

reason.description: Human-readable justification for the exemption. Surfaced to reviewers; should explain why this specific narrowing violation is intentional.

allow_dynamic_refs.description: When true, the publishing-linter accepts $dynamicRef / $dynamicAnchor JSON Schema constructs in catalog content. Default false; these constructs are discouraged because they make compile-time schema composition non-local.

allow_id_overrides.description: When true, the publishing-linter accepts $id overrides on subschemas within an entity's schema content. Default false; $id overrides break the canonical-identifier-per-schema convention the resolver and the JSON Schema validator both rely on.

allow_non_pascal_schema_names.description: When true, the publishing-linter accepts schema definition names that are not PascalCase. Default false; PascalCase keeps schema names visually distinct from instance-side keys (which are snake_case wire format).

allow_direct_x_aggrega_extensions.description: When true, the build-time discouragement walker accepts x-aggrega-selector and x-aggrega-inject keywords authored directly in schema content. Default false; the recommended authoring path is usesSchema (for dependency sockets) or secretsSchema (for credential bindings), which the schema-composition layer then synthesises into the inline extension form.

allow_nonstandard_names.description: When true, the publishing-linter accepts catalog entity names that do not follow the project's documented naming conventions. Default false; consistent naming is load-bearing for the resolver, the selector engine, and reviewer ergonomics.

PluginRef.description: Reference to a Wasm plugin attached at a workspace-level socket. `uri` identifies the plugin (OCI reference, local path, or registry alias). `function` overrides the socket's default entry function (`mutate`, `validate`, `lint`, `import` per socket); when omitted, the socket's documented default applies.

uri.description: Plugin identifier: OCI reference (e.g. `oci://hub.aggrega.ai/aggrega-team/mutator-bundle@v1`), local filesystem path, or registry alias.

function.description: Optional override for the socket's default entry function. When omitted, the socket's documented default applies (mutator → `mutate`, policy → `validate`, linter → `lint`, importer → `import`).
